title: Agent Policy Lab canonical event — v0.2
description: Normalized event shape for coding-agent session traces (Claude Code, Copilot, OpenCode). Companion schema experiment_run.schema.json carries run/experiment-arm lineage (condition, policy, model, task, pinned commit) — deliberately NOT duplicated per event; every event's run_id is a foreign key into it. v0.2.0 adds source_client 'codex-cli'. Client capability differences are preserved EXPLICITLY rather than smoothed: several conditionals below force Codex fields to null/unavailable where Codex genuinely cannot observe them, so an adapter cannot accidentally present a Codex event as richer than the client is. Claude Code stays on 0.1.1 (schema/v0.1); versions are never pooled.

event_id.description: Deterministic UUIDv5 — NOT random, and not copied from the source. Namespace: 64f66254-faf2-5c58-9026-b9af6abf735c (itself uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, 'agent-policy-lab.local'), so it is reproducible rather than a magic constant). Name: the four-tuple (source_client, session_id, line_or_offset, json_pointer) joined by '|', with an empty string for a null json_pointer. Re-ingesting the same session MUST yield identical event_ids; a random id would silently duplicate every event on any re-run after an adapter fix.

sequence_index.description: Monotonic, unique within session_id — a total order across every event in the session. NOT the same as turn_index: multiple events (e.g. several tool_call/tool_result pairs) can share one turn_index, but sequence_index never repeats. Added 0.1.0 review pass: turn_index alone under-specified ordering.

run_id.description: Foreign key into experiment_run.schema.json. Without this, events cannot be reliably joined to a treatment arm (condition, policy_id/version, model, task, pinned commit) — added on review; the original 0.1 draft omitted run lineage entirely.

source_client.description: 'codex-cli' added in 0.2.0. Per-client observability differs materially and is enforced below, not assumed.

session_id.description: Raw locally; MUST be replaced with a salted sha256 hash before any Tier 2 (public) export.

repo_ref.description: Local: hash of absolute path. Public: repo URL + pinned commit. Never a raw local path in a Tier 2 export.

turn_index.description:
Agent input cycle, 0-based. AUTHORITY IS PER CLIENT — the source of a turn boundary is a client fact, not a universal rule:
- claude-code: a raw user record whose promptSource is one of typed/suggestion_accepted/system/sdk. A promptId-only envelope is NOT a turn (see 0.1.1's correction, which cost 391 tool results to discover).
- codex-cli: the native 'task_started' event_msg record, which is unambiguous and requires no inference. Codex user_message events MUST NOT be used to count turns: a single task_started turn may contain several protocol-level user messages, and the corpus shows 587 role:user records against 366 UserMessage items with ZERO shared ids.

event_type.description: subagent_spawn was REMOVED from this enum during the initial fixture pass. Zero instances exist across the ~66 local Claude Code sessions surveyed — no isSidechain:true line, no Task tool_use call — so its real source shape is unknown and no adapter can map it honestly. Deferred to v0.2, pending a controlled/public fixture that demonstrates the actual shape. Do not re-add it from vendor documentation alone.

event_origin.description: Whether this event corresponds to a real record in the source trace ('observed') or was constructed by the adapter because the client emits no such record ('synthesized'). Claude Code has NO native session_start/session_end marker in any surveyed session (first/last raw lines were last-prompt and system/turn_duration), so those events are adapter constructions and must never be counted as observed facts. A synthesized event MUST carry synthesis_reason.

synthesis_reason.description: Required (non-empty) when event_origin == 'synthesized' — states why the adapter constructed this event and from what, e.g. 'no native session_end marker in Claude Code JSONL; synthesized from last line timestamp'. Must be null or absent when event_origin == 'observed'.

raw_source_ref.description: Tier 1 (local) only. MUST be stripped entirely before any Tier 2 (public) export.

line_or_offset.description: Locates the raw record within the source file (for JSONL, the line). Retained as-is — json_pointer addresses WITHIN that record, it does not replace this.

json_pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the specific nested node within the raw record this event was derived from, e.g. '/message/content/2' for the third content block. Null for whole-line events. Claude Code packs tool_call/tool_result/thinking as blocks inside one line's message.content[] array, so a single raw line commonly explodes into 2-3 canonical events — line number alone makes their provenance refs collide. Deliberately a generic pointer rather than a Claude-specific block_index, so other clients' nesting layouts are addressable by the same field.

field_status.description: Maps every variable field present in this event's type-specific payload to its provenance status. A field absent here MUST NOT appear elsewhere in the event. LIMITATION: JSON Schema cannot fully cross-check 'every populated field in tool_call/tool_result/thinking has a matching key here' — the allOf conditionals below enforce that field_status is non-empty when a typed payload is present, but complete per-field cross-validation requires a validator function at adapter/ingestion time, not pure JSON Schema. Do not describe this map as fully mechanically enforced until that validator exists.

additionalProperties.description: 'inferred' covers any value derived rather than directly observed — including a line_range or size reconstructed from partial data. tool_result.result_size_method (below) uses a separate, more specific vocabulary (direct/reconstructed_from_range/unavailable) scoped to size measurement only; do not conflate the two enums.

tool_call.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == tool_call — enforced by the allOf conditionals below.

tool_correlation_id.description: Links this call to its tool_result. MUST be a per-session salted HMAC of the source's tool_use id — never the raw client id, which would leak a source identifier into Tier 2. Equality is the only property that matters, and per-session salting keeps it meaningful within a session while preventing cross-session correlation. field_status is 'inferred', not 'observed': the relationship is observed, this representation of it is derived. Pairing was exact across the surveyed corpus (936 calls / 936 results / 0 orphans / 0 duplicates over 8 sessions), but that is not assumed — an interrupted session may produce a call with no result, in which case the call is emitted with the result simply absent and the adapter reports unmatched counts. Never synthesize a placeholder result. DERIVATION (required for reproducible re-ingestion): HMAC-SHA256(key=local_secret, msg=source_client || session_id || raw_tool_use_id), where local_secret is PERSISTENT Tier 1 configuration — generated once, stored outside the repo, gitignored, never exported. A fresh random salt per run would give the same session two different correlation ids on two ingestions, silently breaking the very join this field exists to provide. session_id sits in the message (not only the key) so a single stable secret still cannot correlate across sessions.

target_path.description: Tier 1: a normalized REPO-RELATIVE path — real enough to check git state for the clean-file pattern, with no home-directory prefix to leak. A path outside the repository, or one that cannot be safely normalized (symlink escape, '..' traversal beyond the root), is set null with field_status 'unavailable' rather than stored absolute. Tier 2 drops this field entirely.

args_digest.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the UTF-8 encoding of the source tool-input object serialized as RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785). A named portable standard, chosen deliberately over an ad-hoc 'sorted keys' rule, which is language-specific and ambiguous about number formatting, unicode escaping, and key ordering. Same reproducibility discipline as result_size_value's canonicalization rule. Normalization-layer summary, not a privacy control — raw args live in raw_source_ref (Tier 1 only).

tool_result.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == tool_result — enforced by the allOf conditionals below.

tool_correlation_id.description: Links this result back to its tool_call — same per-session salted HMAC construction and same 'inferred' status as the tool_call side. Null with field_status 'unavailable' for a result whose originating call was not observed. Same HMAC derivation as the tool_call side; see there.

result_size_value.description: Size in result_size_unit (UTF-8 bytes). CANONICALIZATION RULE, so string- and array-shaped results are not pooled apples-to-oranges: measure the UTF-8 byte length of the source's TEXT content after documented block extraction. Claude Code's tool_result.content is a bare string in ~92% of sampled blocks and an array of typed blocks in the rest; for the array form, extract the text-typed blocks' text in order and concatenate with no separator, then measure. Non-text blocks (images etc.) contribute 0 bytes and force field_status 'inferred' for this field, since their real payload size is not represented.

result_size_unit.description: Only supported unit in v0.1. Present as an explicit const rather than an implicit convention so a future line-based or token-based measure cannot silently reuse result_size_value's meaning.

result_size_method.description: MUST be reconstructed_from_range for any Copilot read_file result — tool_response is empty string on every observed payload (verified live against real payloads, 2026-08-01). direct and reconstructed_from_range values must never be pooled in one statistic without this method traveling with the number.

tool_result.$comment: All three are required. result_size_unit was previously optional, which defeated the point of making the unit explicit — it could simply be omitted. result_size_value is required but nullable: 'unavailable' must be said out loud (null + field_status 'unavailable'), not expressed by leaving the key out, so every tool result carries an unambiguous size representation.

thinking.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == thinking — enforced by the allOf conditionals below. Content itself is never part of the canonical event. There is no length_status property: the per-field status lives in the envelope's field_status map, like every other variable field. CODEX: reasoning is present-but-OPAQUE. Codex emits reasoning records carrying encrypted_content (ciphertext, whose length is not plaintext length) and a summary that is empty in 2,533 of 2,546 corpus records and non-empty in 13. A thinking event IS emitted for each observed reasoning record — the event's existence is observed — but length_value is null with field_status 'unavailable', enforced below. Summary text, when present, stays raw-local (Tier 1) and is never copied into the canonical event, same as Claude Code's plaintext.

length_value.description: UTF-8 byte length of the thinking block's text, same canonicalization as tool_result.result_size_value. Claude Code emits thinking blocks whose .thinking string may be empty with a populated .signature — an empty-but-present block is length_value 0 with field_status 'observed', NOT 'unavailable'.

assistant_message.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == assistant_message. Per-message token usage is verified-observed for this client, but the envelope originally had no payload to hold it, so an adapter would have had to discard it. CRITICAL EMISSION RULE: exactly ONE assistant_message event per raw assistant response. A raw response commonly explodes into several events (thinking + text + N tool_use blocks); attaching this usage block to each of them would multiply-count the response's tokens. The usage belongs to the response envelope, not to any individual content block. Two-sided enforcement: the dataset validator enforces AT MOST ONE assistant_message event per raw source line (no double-count), and the raw-fixture adapter tests assert EXACTLY ONE per normalized assistant source line (no silent drop — 'at most one' is satisfied by zero, which would discard a response's tokens and still pass). CODEX: all four usage fields are null with field_status 'unavailable', enforced below. Codex reports tokens in a separate cumulative event_msg/token_count stream (last_token_usage, total_token_usage) with no 1:1 response correspondence — 2,821 such records against 2,068 messages. Inferring a per-response join from it is forbidden: an unproven join presented as a token number is exactly the smoothing that a field a client cannot honestly populate must never receive.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: The flat top-level number only. The real source block also nests iterations[], server_tool_use, cache_creation{ephemeral_1h,ephemeral_5m}, service_tier and speed; v0.1 deliberately takes none of those. Adding them later is a v0.2 decision, not an adapter improvisation.

user_message.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == user_message. Carries prompt_source so later analysis can distinguish human, SDK, suggestion, and system-originated turns without redefining turn_index. CODEX SEMANTICS, fixed in 0.2.0: a codex-cli user_message means exactly one protocol-level response_item with role 'user'. It does NOT mean one human prompt and does NOT mean one turn. Several may occur within one task_started turn. prompt_source is 'unavailable' for codex-cli — the client has no analogue. The adapter MUST NOT attempt to join these to item_completed/UserMessage records (disjoint id spaces), and no artifact may use Codex user_message counts as prompt counts or turn counts.

prompt_source.description: Observed vocabulary across the surveyed corpus: typed (498), suggestion_accepted (49), system (4), sdk (2). All four open a turn — see turn_index. A value outside this enum means the client introduced a new prompt source and MUST fail rather than be coerced to null; that is the same fail-loudly discipline as an unrecognized raw record type. Always null for codex-cli, enforced below.

compaction.description: Required when (and only when) event_type == compaction — enforced by the allOf conditionals below. compaction is real, observed, and directly relevant to agent-context behavior, but v0.1 originally defined no payload for it, so genuinely observed data had nowhere to go. NEVER carries the compacted summary text — that is raw content, Tier 1 only, reachable via raw_source_ref.

compaction_source.description: Discriminator for which raw record this event came from — Claude Code emits TWO distinct records per compaction and they must not be conflated. 'boundary_marker': a system line with subtype 'compact_boundary', which carries the real compactMetadata numbers. 'continuation_summary': a user line with isCompactSummary true, which carries the resulting summary text (never copied here) and NO metrics. 'unavailable': client signals a compaction occurred with no distinguishable source record. CODEX, 0.2.0: use 'unavailable' with all metrics null until the 'compacted' wrapper payload is separately characterized. No Codex-specific enum value is invented now — a discriminator guessed before its payload is inspected is the same mistake as building an adapter from vendor docs. Codex compaction is nonetheless event_origin 'observed': the 12 ContextCompaction items are real records, only their metrics are uncharacterized.

trigger.description: Observed on Claude Code boundary_marker records as compactMetadata.trigger. Null/unavailable on continuation_summary records — do not infer it from the sibling record; a separate event carries that.

cumulative_dropped_tokens.description: Observed on newer Claude Code versions only — absent from 2.1.150-era boundary records that carry pre/post_tokens and durationMs but no cumulative field. Omit (with field_status 'unavailable') rather than computing it from pre/post, which would be a different quantity presented as observed.

allOf.$comment: event_type 'tool_call' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.

event_type 'tool_result' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.

event_type 'thinking' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.

event_type 'compaction' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.

event_type 'assistant_message' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.

event_type 'user_message' requires its own payload and forbids ALL 5 others. Generated exhaustively rather than hand-maintained: this exclusivity drifted twice during development because adding a payload type means updating every pre-existing branch, which is easy to miss by hand.
session_start/session_end carry no typed payload of any kind.
Partial mechanical enforcement of field_status non-emptiness — per-field cross-validation is a dataset-level concern, see the field_status description.
a synthesized event cannot be emitted without stating why it was constructed — closes 'no synthesized claim can be mistaken for observed data'.
an observed event must not carry a synthesis rationale.

Fixture-derived: Claude Code emits no native session_start/session_end record in any surveyed session, so a claude-code event of either type claiming event_origin 'observed' is provably false and must fail validation. Scoped to claude-code deliberately — another client may genuinely observe these, and that is a per-client fact for the capability matrix, not a global assumption.
0.2.0: codex-cli has no promptSource analogue. Forcing null stops an adapter from inventing one, and stops a Codex user_message from being read as a human prompt.
0.2.0: Codex token usage is a separate cumulative stream with no per-response mapping. Any non-null value here would be an inferred join presented as observed.
0.2.0: Codex reasoning content is encrypted; ciphertext length is not plaintext length, so no honest length exists. The event is still emitted — presence is observed, size is not.
0.2.0: the Codex 'compacted' wrapper payload is not yet characterized, so its metrics are unavailable and its source discriminator is 'unavailable' rather than a guessed new enum value.

0.2.0, evidence-backed: Codex emits a native session_meta record in 98/98 corpus files, so a codex-cli session_start is genuinely observed — the mirror image of claude-code, where the same event must be synthesized. This is why the claude-code conditional was scoped per client.
